title: IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026: Apply for a USD 1,000 Reporting Grant in Chiang Rai, Thailand
summary: Applications are open for the IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026 , a three-month reporting initiative designed to support original, accurate, evidence-based and ethically produced journalism about migration in Chiang Rai and surrounding areas of northern Thailand. Organized by the International Organization for Migration in Thailand, the programme will select five fellows , each of whom will receive a USD 1,000 reporting grant alongside professional mentorship, editorial guidance, programme check-ins, a field visit and potential publication through IOM platforms. The fellowship will run from 1 October to 31 December 2026 , while completed stories must be submitted by 8 January 2027 . Applications must be submitted no later than 22 September 2026 . The official announcement does not specify a closing time, so candidates should avoid waiting until the final day. Review the official IOM Thailand announcement . About the Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme Migration is an important part of Thailand’s social, economic and demographic landscape. Its significance is particularly visible in Chiang Rai, a northern border province where communities, economies and personal experiences are closely connected to cross-border mobility. Despite the importance of migration, public discussion can sometimes be shaped by incomplete information, stereotypes, sensational reporting or narratives that fail to reflect the realities and contributions of migrants. Journalism plays a significant role in determining how migration is understood by communities, institutions and policymakers. The Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme seeks to strengthen the ability of local journalists and emerging media practitioners to produce reporting that is: Accurate and based on credible evidence. Balanced in its treatment of complex migration issues. Sensitive to the dignity, safety and rights of migrants. Connected to the realities of Chiang Rai and surrounding areas. Constructive in how it contributes to public understanding. Professionally and ethically produced. Capable of challenging stereotypes and misleading migration narratives. The programme’s central theme is the reframing of migration narratives and public perceptions to encourage greater inclusion of migrants. Through well-researched stories grounded in evidence, local realities and migrants’ experiences, fellows are expected to help build a more informed and constructive understanding of migration at the local level. Read the official call for proposals . The initiative is made possible through financial support from the Government of Japan . See the programme announcement from IOM Thailand . Main Objectives of the Programme The fellowship is intended to move beyond short-term awareness raising by providing selected participants with practical support to research, produce and complete substantial migration stories. Its main objectives include: Supporting local migration journalism The programme provides financial and professional assistance for reporting on migration issues connected to Chiang Rai and nearby areas. Improving the accuracy of migration reporting Fellows will be encouraged to use reliable evidence, appropriate sources and properly verified information when developing their stories. Promoting balanced and ethical storytelling The programme emphasizes journalism that avoids harmful stereotypes, respects the dignity of migrants and accurately represents complex migration experiences. Connecting national migration issues with local realities Proposed stories should be relevant to Chiang Rai or its surrounding areas rather than addressing migration only as a broad or abstract international issue. Strengthening the practical capacity of journalists and emerging storytellers Through mentorship, editorial guidance, orientation sessions and programme check-ins, fellows will receive structured support throughout the reporting process. Expanding public access to evidence-based migration stories Completed work may be published through IOM platforms, giving selected fellows an opportunity to reach wider audiences. What Selected Fellows Will Receive 1. USD 1,000 Reporting Grant Each of the five selected fellows will receive a reporting grant of USD 1,000 to support the production of an original migration story. The grant is intended to assist with the reporting and production process. Applicants should therefore present a story idea that is realistic, properly planned and achievable within the available funding and programme period. This is a reporting grant rather than a salary, academic scholarship or general cash award. It is connected to the successful production of the proposed journalism project. See IOM Thailand’s official fellowship information . 2. Professional Mentorship Selected fellows will receive mentorship while developing their stories. This support can help participants strengthen their research plans, refine their angles, address gaps in evidence and improve the overall quality of their reporting. Mentorship is especially valuable for participants working on sensitive migration topics that require careful consideration of informed consent, confidentiality, source protection, representation and the potential consequences of publication. 3. Editorial Guidance IOM and designated mentors will provide editorial feedback during the reporting process. Fellows will be expected to respond constructively to this guidance and incorporate relevant recommendations into their work. Editorial support may help participants improve the structure, clarity, factual accuracy, balance and ethical quality of their final stories. 4. Online Orientation and Monthly Check-Ins Selected participants will take part in an online orientation session at the beginning of the programme. IOM will also organize monthly check-ins throughout the fellowship period. These sessions are intended to monitor progress, provide guidance, identify emerging challenges and help fellows remain on schedule. 5. Field Visit in Chiang Rai The programme includes a field visit within Chiang Rai organized by IOM. The field visit is designed to deepen participants’ understanding of migration dynamics in the province. It will also provide opportunities to exchange experiences with foreign correspondents and other relevant stakeholders. Consult the official call for the participation requirements . 6. Opportunity for Publication Fellows may have their completed stories published through IOM platforms. Publication can increase the visibility of the participant’s work while contributing to broader public understanding of migration. It may also strengthen the fellow’s professional portfolio and demonstrate an ability to produce responsible, evidence-based reporting on a complex social issue. Publication is not automatic or unconditional. Materials developed through the programme will be reviewed by IOM before they are published or otherwise disseminated. Expected Journalism Project Applicants must propose an original and feasible story related to migration in Chiang Rai and/or surrounding areas . A strong project should establish a clear connection between the proposed subject and the local migration context. The idea should be narrow enough to investigate properly within the programme period but significant enough to contribute meaningfully to public understanding. The proposed story should ultimately demonstrate: A clearly defined migration issue or reporting question. Relevance to Chiang Rai or surrounding communities. A practical reporting and production plan. Credible sources and evidence. Appropriate inclusion of migrant experiences and perspectives. Balanced treatment of the people and institutions involved. Ethical interviewing and reporting practices. Realistic completion within the three-month fellowship. Responsiveness to editorial feedback. Compliance with the final format and supporting-material requirements established by IOM. Applicants should avoid submitting broad proposals that attempt to cover every dimension of migration. A focused story with identifiable sources, a clear audience and a realistic reporting plan is more likely to be completed effectively. Responsibilities of Selected Fellows Receiving the grant carries clear professional and programme obligations. Successful applicants will be expected to: Produce a high-quality migration story by the agreed deadline. Participate in the programme’s online orientation. Attend monthly check-ins organized by IOM. Participate in the IOM-organized field visit in Chiang Rai. Remain engaged throughout the fellowship period. Incorporate appropriate editorial guidance from IOM or designated mentors. Complete the proposed story within the approved timeline. Follow applicable professional and ethical journalism standards. Submit all required supporting materials with the final story. Ensure that the completed work meets the minimum format requirements stated in the programme documents. Submit the final story by 8 January 2027 . All materials produced through the programme will be subject to IOM review and approval before publication or dissemination. This review is intended to confirm that funded stories remain within the approved scope, meet ethical and professional standards and comply with relevant IOM requirements. Read the official terms in the call for proposals . Documents Required for the Application Applicants should prepare the complete application package before opening the online submission form. The required materials include: 1. Updated Resume or CV The resume or CV should clearly present the applicant’s education, journalism or media experience, relevant training, publications, reporting interests and other experience connected to migration, social issues or public-interest communication. 2. Cover Letter Applicants must provide a cover letter explaining: Their motivation for applying. Their interest in ethical migration journalism. Their proposed story idea. Why the subject is relevant to Chiang Rai or surrounding areas. How they intend to complete the project. The cover letter and proposed story description should be concise and should not exceed one page . 3. Completed Story Proposal Form Candidates must download and complete the official Story Proposal Form available through the programme webpage. The proposal should be internally consistent with the information provided in the cover letter and online application form. 4. Certificate of Relevant IOM Training Applicants must provide evidence that they completed the qualifying IOM training or e-learning route. For the e-learning route, both the Migration Explained and Reporting Migration in Thailand modules must be completed. 5. Previous Work Samples Journalist applicants must provide two relevant samples of previous work . This requirement is specifically identified for journalist applicants. The samples should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to research, structure and communicate a story professionally. Whenever possible, applicants should select work relevant to migration, human rights, border communities, social inclusion or another complex public-interest issue. Confirm the complete application requirements on the official IOM page . How to Apply Interested candidates should follow these steps: Review the official programme announcement and call for proposals. Confirm that all location and training requirements are met. Develop an original and feasible migration story connected to Chiang Rai or surrounding areas. Update the resume or CV. Prepare a focused cover letter of no more than one page. Download and complete the official Story Proposal Form. Obtain the certificate showing completion of the required training or e-learning modules. Prepare two relevant work samples if applying as a journalist. Complete the online application form available through the official IOM Thailand programme page. Submit the entire application no later than 22 September 2026 . Apply through the official IOM Thailand opportunity page Candidates should carefully check uploaded documents before submitting. The story title, subject, proposed activities and timeline should remain consistent across the cover letter, proposal form and online application. Important Programme Dates Programme stage Date Applications opened 1 September 2026 Application deadline 22 September 2026 Shortlisting and interviews 23–25 September 2026 Selection announcement 29 September 2026 Fellowship period 1 October–31 December 2026 Final story submission 8 January 2027 The short period between the application deadline and interviews means applicants should remain available and regularly monitor the email address and telephone number provided in their application. How to Prepare a Strong Story Proposal Although applicants should follow the official Story Proposal Form, the following practical steps can help produce a clearer and more competitive submission. Define a Focused Local Issue Identify a specific migration-related issue that can be examined within Chiang Rai or nearby areas. Avoid a subject that is too broad to research properly within three months. Explain Why the Story Matters Clearly describe why the proposed story is relevant to local communities and how it could improve public understanding of migration. Present a Credible Reporting Plan Explain which people, communities, experts, institutions, documents and other sources may be consulted. Applicants should demonstrate that the proposed reporting process is realistic. Center Accuracy and Ethics The proposal should explain how information will be verified and how the dignity, privacy and safety of migrants or other potentially vulnerable sources will be protected. Include Migrant Perspectives Responsibly Migration stories should not treat migrants only as statistics or passive subjects. Where appropriate and safe, the proposal should create space for migrants to explain their experiences in their own words. Demonstrate Feasibility The reporting scope, production method and expected output should be achievable between October and December 2026 and within the USD 1,000 grant. Prepare for Editorial Collaboration Applicants should demonstrate openness to mentorship, review and constructive editorial feedback. The fellowship is structured as a supported reporting process rather than an unrestricted financial award. Review Every Document for Consistency The CV, cover letter, proposal form, work samples and online application should support the same professional narrative. Conflicting titles, timelines or project descriptions could weaken the application. Contact for Questions Questions about the programme or application process may be directed to: Email: mediathailand@iom.int Applicants should first review the official announcement and call for proposals before contacting IOM. Questions should be clear, specific and directly related to information not already addressed in the published materials. Application Deadline The application deadline is: 22 September 2026 No specific closing time or time zone is stated in the accessible programme announcement. Applicants should submit early to avoid technical problems or uncertainty on the final day. Conclusion The IOM Ethical Migration Journalism Fellowship Programme 2026 offers an important opportunity to transform a strong local story idea into professionally supported, evidence-based journalism. Five selected fellows will receive USD 1,000 each, along with mentorship, editorial guidance, structured check-ins, a field visit in Chiang Rai and potential publication through IOM platforms. More importantly, participants will contribute to a wider effort to improve how migration is reported and understood in northern Thailand. This is a project-based programme with meaningful responsibilities. A successful fellow must be prepared to conduct careful research, engage ethically with sources, respond to editorial feedback and submit a completed story by 8 January 2027. Interested candidates should prepare their application documents carefully and submit the online form by 22 September 2026 . For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: WIPO Internship 2027 in Geneva: Paid Economics, Data Science and Innovation Research Internship at WIPO
summary: The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is inviting applications for a Category II Internship within its Composite Indicator Research Section, Department for Economics and Data Analytics (DEDA), under the IP and Innovation Ecosystems Sector (IES). This six-month internship will be based at WIPO Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland , and is designed for qualified candidates with an academic background in economics, data science or a related field who have strong interests in statistical analysis, econometrics, data visualization, innovation economics and policy research. The selected intern will contribute to major WIPO research publications, including the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2027 and the World Intangible Investment Highlights (WIIH) 2027 . The internship is expected to begin on January 4, 2027 , and provides a monthly stipend of CHF 2,170 , together with medical insurance, annual leave and sick leave benefits. The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST . About the WIPO Internship Program The WIPO Internship Program is designed to help students and recent graduates complement their academic education with practical professional experience in an international organisation. Through participation in the workplace, interns can apply their academic knowledge to real-world projects while developing professional skills and competencies. The programme also provides opportunities for learning through: Practical work experience. Exposure to an international working environment. Supervision and feedback from experienced colleagues. Technical mentoring. Structured courses and learning programmes where available. Experience working within the United Nations common system. For candidates interested in international organisations, economics, innovation, data analytics and public policy, this internship provides an opportunity to gain practical experience while working on internationally relevant research and publications. About the Host Department This internship is hosted by the Composite Indicator Research Section within the Department for Economics and Data Analytics (DEDA) of WIPO s IP and Innovation Ecosystems Sector (IES) . The intern will work under the supervision of the Head of the Composite Indicator Research Section . The section s work involves economic and data analysis, including research associated with innovation and intangible investment. The internship therefore combines several areas, including: Economics Statistics Data analytics Econometrics Innovation research Economic publications Data visualization Policy research Digital communications Main Objectives of the Internship The internship has several key objectives. APPLY HERE Apply Academic Knowledge The intern will have an opportunity to apply knowledge of economics, statistics and data analytics to practical work involving economic publications and policymaking. This means the internship is not purely administrative. Candidates will be expected to contribute analytical skills to research and publication-related activities. Receive Technical Supervision and Mentoring The intern will work under the guidance of experienced WIPO staff. This provides an opportunity to receive technical supervision and mentoring while developing practical research and analytical skills. Gain United Nations System Experience The internship provides experience working within a United Nations common system organization . This can give successful candidates exposure to the working environment, processes and professional standards of an international organisation. Key Research Projects The successful intern will contribute to work associated with two major publications. Global Innovation Index 2027 One of the primary areas of work will be the Global Innovation Index (GII) 2027 . The Global Innovation Index is associated with research and analysis concerning innovation performance. The intern may contribute analytical inputs and other research-related activities supporting the preparation of the 2027 edition. This can provide practical experience in using data and economic analysis to support an internationally recognised research publication. World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027 The intern will also contribute to the World Intangible Investment Highlights (WIIH) 2027 . This work focuses on measuring investment in intangible assets and communicating findings through research publications and related materials. The combination of the GII and WIIH projects means that the intern can gain exposure to economic research, data analysis, innovation and intangible investment. Duties and Responsibilities Under the supervision of the Head of the Composite Indicator Research Section, the intern will contribute to several areas of work. 1. Research and Analytical Contributions The intern will provide analytical inputs to the production of: Global Innovation Index 2027. World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027. This may involve working with economic and statistical information and supporting research used in the preparation of the publications. 2. Data Visualization The intern will provide support for data visualization . This is particularly relevant for candidates interested in communicating complex datasets and economic findings through clear and accessible visual formats. Applicants with experience using modern data visualization tools may therefore have an advantage. 3. Social Media and Website Content The intern will also support the preparation of content for: WIPO s social media platforms. The WIPO website. This work will be carried out under editorial guidance. Candidates with experience creating digital content, drafting web content or preparing social media materials may therefore find this aspect of the internship particularly relevant. 4. Event Organisation The intern will assist with the organisation of events connected to the two major publications. Responsibilities may include preparing: Presentations. Talking points. Background materials. Other event-related documentation. This provides exposure to the communication and event-management side of international research projects. 5. Logistical and Administrative Support The intern may also perform other related tasks as required. Examples include: Drafting invitations. Coordinating event logistics. Supporting administrative processes. Providing general logistical assistance related to research activities and events. The internship therefore combines analytical, communication, research and organisational responsibilities. Educational Requirements The essential educational requirement is an: Advanced university degree (master s degree) in economics, data science or a related field. Candidates should therefore have an appropriate postgraduate academic background relevant to the work of the Composite Indicator Research Section. Relevant academic areas may include economics, data science and related disciplines where the candidate has developed strong quantitative, analytical or research capabilities. Statistical and Programming Experience Applicants must have experience using specialised software and programming languages for statistical or econometric analysis . The announcement specifically highlights: R Python Experience with either R, Python or both is therefore particularly relevant to the position. Candidates should be able to demonstrate practical experience using these tools for statistical analysis, econometric work, data processing or related research activities. Data Visualization Skills Familiarity with modern data visualization tools is an essential requirement. Applicants should also have an interest in developing their data visualization skills further. This suggests that candidates should be comfortable working with data and interested in transforming analytical findings into understandable visual outputs. Desirable Skills and Experience Several additional qualifications are listed as desirable rather than essential. These include: Applied Economics Knowledge of or experience with applied economics is an advantage. Candidates with experience applying economic concepts and analytical methods to real-world economic questions may therefore be particularly well suited. Innovation Economics Experience or knowledge of innovation economics is also desirable. This is particularly relevant given the internship s connection to the Global Innovation Index and WIPO s broader work on innovation ecosystems. Social Media and Web Content Experience drafting content for social media and web use is another advantage. Candidates who can combine technical research skills with strong digital communication abilities may therefore be able to contribute across several areas of the internship. Communication Skills The position also values: Strong oral communication. Strong written communication. Strong interpersonal skills. The ability to communicate effectively is important because the intern will contribute to research publications, digital content, presentations and events. Multicultural Working Environment Candidates should have the ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment . Because WIPO is an international organisation, interns are expected to work respectfully and effectively with colleagues from different professional, cultural and national backgrounds. Professional Integrity Sound judgement and integrity are also listed among the desirable competencies. Language Requirements Excellent written and spoken English is an essential requirement. Candidates must therefore be able to communicate effectively in English in both professional and written settings. Knowledge of other official United Nations languages is desirable. Additional UN languages may therefore strengthen an applicant s profile, although they are not listed as essential. Organisational Competencies WIPO identifies several organisational competencies relevant to the internship. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to: Communicate effectively Show team spirit Demonstrate integrity Value diversity Produce results Show service orientation See the big picture Seek change and innovation Develop yourself and others These competencies reflect the professional behaviours expected within the organisation. Internship Duration The internship has an expected duration of: Six months The internship may be renewed, subject to the applicable conditions. The minimum duration is six months, while the maximum total duration is 12 months . Expected Start Date The expected start date is: January 4, 2027 Candidates should therefore be prepared to undertake the internship from this date if selected. Location and Remote Work The internship will take place at: WIPO Headquarters, Geneva, Switzerland Importantly, this internship cannot be carried out remotely . The selected candidate will therefore need to work physically from WIPO s headquarters in Geneva. Internship Working Hours The stipend stated in the vacancy is based on a full-time internship of 40 hours per week . Candidates should therefore be prepared to commit to a full-time schedule for the duration of the internship. Stipend and Benefits The selected intern will receive a monthly stipend of: CHF 2,170 In addition to the stipend, the internship provides: Medical insurance. Annual leave. Sick leave benefits. The stipend amount applies to the full-time 40-hour-per-week internship. The internship is therefore a paid opportunity rather than an unpaid placement. Eligibility Requirements This position falls under Category II of the WIPO Internship Program . Under the eligibility rules provided in the opportunity, the following individuals may qualify: Category II Eligibility Option A: Students Pursuing Their First Advanced University Degree Individuals who are pursuing their first advanced university degree may qualify if they have: Completed their coursework. Not yet completed their final thesis. Option B: Individuals Pursuing a Subsequent Degree Individuals who have already obtained their first advanced university degree and are currently pursuing a subsequent university degree may also qualify. Option C: Recent Advanced Degree Graduates Individuals who obtained their most recent advanced university degree less than two years before the date of their internship application may also qualify. Applicants should carefully determine which of these three categories applies to their situation before applying. Who Should Apply? The internship is particularly suited to candidates who combine postgraduate academic training with practical quantitative and analytical skills. A competitive candidate would ideally have: A master s degree or qualifying advanced university degree in economics, data science or a related field. Experience with R and/or Python. Experience in statistical or econometric analysis. Familiarity with modern data visualization tools. Excellent written and spoken English. An interest in economics, innovation, data analytics and policy research. Strong communication skills. Strong interpersonal skills. The ability to work in a multicultural environment. Additional experience in applied economics, innovation economics, social media, web content and data communication would be advantageous. Application Requirements Applicants must submit two essential documents : 1. Motivation Letter The motivation letter should explain the candidate s interest in the internship and demonstrate their suitability for the position. Candidates should use the letter to connect their academic background, technical skills and professional interests with the work of the Composite Indicator Research Section. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must also submit a current CV. The CV should clearly present relevant: Educational qualifications. Research experience. Statistical and econometric experience. Programming skills. Data visualization experience. Professional experience. Communication and digital-content experience. Important LinkedIn Application Requirement Candidates applying through LinkedIn using Easy Apply should pay particular attention to the document-upload requirement. The CV and cover letter must be combined into one single PDF file when submitting through LinkedIn Easy Apply. Applicants should not upload them as separate documents if using the Easy Apply route. Most importantly, applications that do not include both a motivation letter and a curriculum vitae will not be considered . Visit HERE to learn more about the WIPO Internship 2027 in Geneva Application Deadline The application deadline is: September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST Candidates should ensure that all required application materials are submitted before the deadline. Because applications missing either the motivation letter or CV will not be considered, applicants should verify their submission carefully before sending it. Application Process Interested candidates should: Review the eligibility requirements for Category II internships. Confirm that they meet the educational and technical requirements. Prepare a motivation letter. Prepare an up-to-date CV. If applying through LinkedIn Easy Apply, combine the CV and motivation letter into one PDF. Submit the required documents to gii@wipo.int . Ensure the application is submitted before September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST . Key Facts at a Glance Detail Information Organisation World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Internship area Composite Indicator Research Department Economics and Data Analytics Sector IP and Innovation Ecosystems Location Geneva, Switzerland Internship type Category II Duration 6 months, renewable up to 12 months Start date January 4, 2027 Working arrangement Full-time, on-site Working hours 40 hours per week Monthly stipend CHF 2,170 Medical insurance Provided Annual leave Provided Sick leave Provided Main research areas Economics, data analytics, innovation and intangible investment Programming R and/or Python Essential language English Application email gii@wipo.int Deadline September 15, 2026, 11:59 PM CEST Why This WIPO Internship Is Valuable This internship provides an opportunity to gain practical experience at an international organisation while working on research and publications related to innovation, economics and data. The successful intern will gain exposure to several professional areas, including: Economic research. Statistical analysis. Econometric programming. Data visualization. Innovation research. Intangible investment research. Economic publications. International policy work. Digital communication. Event preparation. Working within a multicultural international organisation. The opportunity can therefore be particularly valuable for candidates looking to combine economics or data science with international development, innovation policy and research . Important Points to Remember Before applying, candidates should carefully note the following: The internship is based in Geneva, Switzerland . It is not remote . The expected start date is January 4, 2027 . The internship is full-time, at 40 hours per week . The initial duration is six months . It can be renewed up to a maximum of 12 months . The monthly stipend is CHF 2,170 . Medical insurance is provided. Annual leave and sick leave are provided. A master s degree or qualifying advanced university degree in economics, data science or a related field is required. Experience with R and/or Python is essential. Familiarity with modern data visualization tools is essential. Excellent written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of other UN official languages is an advantage. Applicants must meet the Category II internship eligibility requirements. Both a motivation letter and CV are mandatory. LinkedIn Easy Apply applicants must combine both documents into one PDF. The deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST . Conclusion The WIPO Economics and Data Analytics Internship 2027 offers an excellent opportunity for qualified postgraduate students and recent advanced-degree graduates to gain practical experience in economics, statistics, data analytics, innovation research and international policymaking. Based at WIPO Headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland , the six-month internship will allow the selected candidate to contribute to major publications such as the Global Innovation Index 2027 and World Intangible Investment Highlights 2027 . The position is particularly suited to candidates with expertise in economics or data science, statistical and econometric analysis, R and/or Python, and data visualization . Additional experience in applied economics, innovation economics, social media and web content can further strengthen an application. The successful candidate will receive a CHF 2,170 monthly stipend , medical insurance, annual leave and sick leave. The internship is full-time and on-site, with the possibility of renewal up to a maximum of 12 months. Interested applicants should carefully review the Category II eligibility requirements, prepare their motivation letter and CV, and submit their application before September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM CEST . title: University of Rochester Political Science Professor Job 2027: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Position in Political Methodology
summary: The University of Rochester is inviting applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Political Science specializing in political methodology . The position is based in Rochester, New York, and is expected to begin on July 1, 2027 . The opportunity is offered through the Department of Political Science within the University s School of Arts Sciences. It is particularly suited to scholars whose methodological research addresses substantive questions in politics and political economy . Candidates from political science and related disciplines, including statistics, computer science, and economics , are encouraged to apply, provided their research aligns with the position s methodological and substantive focus. About the Position The Department of Political Science at the University of Rochester is seeking a scholar for a tenure-track faculty appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor . The successful candidate will join the department as a political methodology scholar whose research connects methodological innovation with substantive questions in politics and political economy. The position provides an opportunity for an early-career academic to develop a long-term research and teaching career within a university environment. The appointment is scheduled to begin: July 1, 2027 The position is based in: Rochester, New York, USA The listed salary range is: $120,000–$140,000 What Is Political Methodology? Political methodology is an area of political science concerned with developing and applying research methods to understand political phenomena. Researchers in this field may work with statistical methods, computational approaches, causal inference, research design, data analysis, mathematical modelling and other quantitative or qualitative approaches. For this particular position, the University of Rochester is interested in candidates whose methodological research does not exist independently from substantive political questions. Instead, candidates should demonstrate how their methodological research can be used to investigate important questions relating to politics and political economy . This makes the position particularly relevant to researchers who combine methodological expertise with substantive interests in political science. Research Focus Applicants should have methodological research interests that address substantive questions in: Politics Political economy Political behaviour Political institutions Related areas of political science The department welcomes candidates whose research demonstrates strong methodological expertise while making meaningful contributions to understanding political or economic processes. Applicants from related disciplines may also be considered, particularly where their methodological work connects clearly with political science. Academic Background The position is open to candidates who hold a PhD or are ABD in political science or a related discipline. The advertisement specifically identifies several related fields, including: Statistics Computer science Economics Other relevant disciplines Candidates from these fields should be able to demonstrate that their methodological research addresses substantive questions relevant to politics and political economy. PhD and ABD Candidates Applicants do not necessarily need to have completed their PhD at the time of application because the position also welcomes candidates who are ABD (All But Dissertation) . However, applicants should have the appropriate doctoral-level academic background in political science or a related field. Candidates should ensure that their academic and research profile demonstrates a strong fit with the department s focus on political methodology. Salary The advertised salary range for the position is: $120,000–$140,000 The final salary may depend on factors such as the candidate s qualifications, experience and the University s applicable compensation policies. Location The position is located in: Rochester, New York Rochester is home to the University of Rochester and provides the academic environment in which the successful candidate will undertake their teaching and research responsibilities. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The University of Rochester will consider all applications received by September 15, 2026 . Importantly, the department states that it will continue accepting applications after September 15, 2026 . Applicants are therefore encouraged to submit their applications by the September 15 priority date rather than waiting until after the stated date. Priority application date: September 15, 2026 Required Application Documents Applicants are required to submit several documents as part of their application. 1. Cover Letter The cover letter should introduce the candidate and explain their suitability for the position. Applicants should use the letter to demonstrate their academic background, research interests and alignment with the Department of Political Science. 2. Curriculum Vitae Candidates must submit an up-to-date CV detailing their academic qualifications, research experience, publications, teaching experience and other relevant professional achievements. 3. Research Statement A research statement is required. This document should communicate the candidate s research agenda, methodological expertise, scholarly contributions and future research plans. Candidates should make the connection between their methodological research and substantive questions in politics or political economy clear. 4. Teaching Statement Applicants must also submit a teaching statement . The statement should provide information about the candidate s teaching experience, approach to teaching and potential contribution to the department s academic programmes. 5. Three Confidential Letters of Recommendation Applicants must arrange for three confidential letters of recommendation to be submitted. These letters should provide an independent assessment of the candidate s academic and research capabilities. 6. Writing Sample A writing sample must also be included in the application. Candidates should select a piece of scholarly work that demonstrates the quality of their research, analytical abilities and methodological expertise. How the Application Process Works The University of Rochester is using Interfolio s Faculty Search system to manage applications for this position. Applicants who apply through Interfolio will receive a free Dossier account . This allows candidates to submit their application materials through the platform, including confidential recommendation letters, without being charged for the dossier service. Applicants should make sure that all required documents are uploaded and that their recommendation letters are properly arranged before submitting their application. Equal Employment Opportunity The University of Rochester states that it is an equal employment opportunity institution, including with respect to disability and protected veteran status . The University is committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming culture that supports its mission to Learn, Discover, Heal, Create – and Make the World Ever Better . The University s nondiscrimination commitment extends to employment, recruitment, admissions and access. The institution states that it does not discriminate on the basis of protected characteristics including: Age Color Disability Ethnicity Gender identity or expression Genetic information Marital status Military or veteran status National origin Race Religion or creed Sex Sexual orientation Citizenship status Other characteristics protected by applicable federal, state or local law Why This Opportunity May Be Valuable for Political Science Researchers This position provides an opportunity for a scholar specializing in political methodology to pursue a tenure-track academic career at the University of Rochester. The role may be particularly attractive to researchers who want to combine methodological expertise with substantive political research. title: UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy 2027: Applications Open for Doctoral Study in the United States
summary: Applications are open for the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy for Fall 2027 , offering prospective doctoral students an opportunity to pursue advanced interdisciplinary study and research focused on some of the most significant domestic and global public policy challenges. Offered through UNC Public Policy in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill , the PhD program is designed for students who want to contribute new knowledge, conduct rigorous policy research, and develop theoretical and analytical approaches that can help address complex public problems. The program combines foundations in theory, empirical research, normative analysis, economics, political science, research design, statistics and specialized policy study. Students can develop expertise across a broad range of fields, including education, innovation and entrepreneurship, labor markets, health and social policy, immigration, environmental policy, national security, international development and global health. Importantly for prospective applicants, GRE scores will not be required or reviewed for the Fall 2027 admissions cycle . The application deadline for Fall 2027 admission is December 1, 2026 . About the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, commonly known as UNC-Chapel Hill or UNC, is located in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States. The PhD in Public Policy is housed within UNC Public Policy in the university s College of Arts and Sciences. The department combines perspectives from multiple social science disciplines to train researchers capable of analyzing important public policy questions. UNC Public Policy s doctoral program has approximately 30 students actively pursuing PhD degrees across a variety of policy interests. Graduate students work closely with faculty members on policy-relevant research and receive extensive training in the theoretical, methodological and substantive foundations necessary for advanced public policy scholarship. About the UNC PhD in Public Policy The UNC PhD in Public Policy is intended for students who want to develop new knowledge about major domestic and global policy problems and contribute to solving them through rigorous research. The program brings together multiple academic disciplines. Its coursework incorporates areas including: Economics Political science Philosophy and normative analysis Research design Statistics and quantitative methods Public policy theory Specialized substantive policy fields Students ultimately undertake doctoral research intended to create new knowledge, social science theory and/or methods that can contribute to understanding significant domestic and international public policy challenges. Graduates are prepared for careers that can include academic appointments, policy research positions, government roles and other positions requiring advanced policy analysis and research expertise. Policy Areas Students Can Explore One of the important features of the UNC Public Policy PhD is the ability for doctoral students to build expertise around their individual policy interests. Potential areas identified by UNC Public Policy include: Education Innovation and entrepreneurship Labor markets Health policy Social policy Immigration Environmental policy National security International development Global health Rather than limiting every doctoral student to the same substantive specialization, the program combines a common methodological and theoretical foundation with an individualized policy field. Students therefore receive broad training in public policy analysis while developing specialized expertise appropriate to their research interests and future careers. Who Is the PhD Program Designed For? The program is particularly relevant to applicants interested in becoming researchers, academics and policy professionals capable of conducting independent scholarly research. UNC states that students enter its doctoral program from diverse backgrounds in academic preparation and experience , and that this diversity is welcomed and encouraged. Although the supplied program requirements do not establish calculus, microeconomics and statistics as admission prerequisites, UNC explains that students who have successfully completed: A first course in calculus Introductory microeconomics Introductory statistics will be best prepared for the program s core curriculum. All entering students are also required to take PLCY 800 , which provides mathematical preparation for economic and statistical analysis. Structure of the UNC PhD in Public Policy The doctoral program follows a structured progression from coursework and field specialization to independent research and dissertation completion. Broadly, students must: Define a policy field. Successfully complete core and policy-field coursework. Receive a passing grade on a field paper written examination. Orally defend a dissertation proposal. Orally defend the completed dissertation. Each stage must be successfully completed before the student proceeds to the next stage. This progression is designed to move students from foundational doctoral training toward increasingly independent research. PhD Coursework Requirements UNC Public Policy requires PhD students to complete 44 credit hours of coursework , consisting of: 26 credit hours of core courses 18 credit hours in a self-defined substantive policy field Students generally undertake two years of full-time coursework. Graduate courses previously completed elsewhere that duplicate required courses may potentially be considered, with students able to petition the Director of Graduate Studies to have up to nine such hours counted toward the PhD, subject to program approval. Core Academic Training The core curriculum provides extensive preparation across politics, institutions, economics, ethics, research design and quantitative methods. Core courses include: PLCY 816 – Politics and Public Policy Theory PLCY 817 – Institutional Analysis for Public Policy PLCY 880 – Normative Dimensions of Public Policy PLCY 888 – Advanced Economic Analysis for Public Policy I PLCY 889 – Advanced Economic Analysis for Public Policy II PLCY 801 – Design of Policy Research PLCY 810 – Public Policy Seminar PLCY 881 / HPM 881 – Linear Regression Models PLCY 882 / HPM 882 – Advanced Panel Data Methodology for Public Policy Together, these core courses account for 26 credit hours. Mathematical Preparation Students entering the program take PLCY 800 Math Camp , an intensive preparation course covering mathematical and statistical analysis relevant to economics and public policy. Topics include: Linear algebra Calculus Optimization Mathematical statistics The course prepares students for advanced economic analysis and quantitative methods courses. Individual Policy Field Specialization In addition to the common core curriculum, every doctoral student develops an individualized substantive policy field. Students work with their academic advisor and relevant faculty members to begin defining their field and planning their coursework during their first year. UNC defines a field as a recognized substantive area of public policy research supported by a coherent body of scholarly literature. The specialization should be sufficiently broad to support a longer-term career in research and teaching rather than being narrowly constructed around a single dissertation topic. The policy specialization requires 18 credit hours , normally consisting of: At least 3 credit hours in research methods At least 9 credit hours in theory and substantive policy content Normally 6 credit hours of doctoral dissertation research through PLCY 994 Students can draw on appropriate graduate-level courses at UNC and neighboring universities, subject to program requirements and approval. Research and Teaching Experience The doctoral experience extends beyond classroom study. According to the program s illustrative course sequencing, many PhD students hold teaching or research assistantship responsibilities of approximately 20 hours per week while completing their studies. Students holding such positions are required to maintain full-time student status. This provides an environment in which doctoral students can combine advanced academic study with research or teaching experience. Prospective applicants should note, however, that the information supplied does not state that an assistantship is automatically guaranteed to every admitted student. Academic Advising Each admitted student is assigned a primary academic advisor upon entering the program . Students may nominate a member of the Public Policy core faculty to serve as their program advisor, and the advisor is generally expected to teach or conduct research in an area related to the student s prospective specialization. The advisor supports the student s academic development throughout the doctoral program. Academic progress is also formally reviewed. Advisors are expected to meet students regularly and at least once per semester, while the Director of Graduate Studies conducts annual progress reviews. Field Paper Written Examination An important milestone in the UNC Public Policy PhD is the field paper written examination . The examination evaluates a student s ability to undertake significant independent academic work. The field paper must be solo-authored and can take forms recognized within public policy scholarship, including: Quantitative empirical research Qualitative empirical research Critical literature review Normative analysis Theoretical analysis Methodological research The paper must be a substantial work of at least 30 double-spaced pages , excluding tables, figures and references. It should demonstrate the student s capacity for independent scholarly activity and meaningfully advance their engagement with their chosen policy field. Students generally begin planning their field paper during their second year and are expected to defend it orally during the fall semester of their third year. Dissertation Research Students who successfully progress through the field paper stage move toward their dissertation proposal. The dissertation must make an original scholarly contribution to a substantive area of public policy . Students are expected to identify a research question with theoretical and/or policy relevance, connect the research to existing scholarship, and employ methods appropriate to the research problem. Dissertations may use: Quantitative research Qualitative research Mixed-methods research The research should ultimately contribute to public policy scholarship, research or practice. The dissertation proposal is developed in collaboration with the student s advisor and committee and must eventually be defended orally. After completing the research and dissertation, the student must undertake a final oral examination. The examination primarily focuses on defending the research and writing contained in the dissertation, although questions may also connect the dissertation to the broader field of public policy. Time Available to Complete the PhD Under UNC regulations, PhD students have a maximum of eight calendar years from their first Graduate School registration to complete their doctoral degree. The program also has residency requirements, including a minimum of four semesters of residency, with at least two earned through continuous registration on the UNC campus. UNC also notes that students are not guaranteed funding beyond their fifth year . Applicants should therefore consider both the academic and financial implications of a multi-year doctoral commitment when preparing to apply. The Hammer Fund for the Enrichment of the PhD Curriculum in Public Policy UNC Public Policy also highlights the Philip and Jane Hammer Fund for the Enrichment of the PhD Curriculum in Public Policy . Established in 1991 by Jane R. Hammer, the fund supports the recruitment and support of exceptional graduate students in the Public Policy PhD program. Prospective applicants interested in funding should review current UNC Public Policy and Graduate School funding information carefully to determine what support may be available for their admission cycle. Career Opportunities After the UNC Public Policy PhD The program is designed to prepare graduates for careers requiring sophisticated research, policy analysis and subject-matter expertise. UNC Public Policy reports that its doctoral graduates have obtained positions in: Universities and academic institutions Policy research organizations Government agencies Public-sector organizations Private-sector organizations Non-profit organizations The program s mission specifically emphasizes preparing graduates to hold academic positions, conduct policy research useful to decision-makers, and advance knowledge within public policy and their chosen substantive fields. Fall 2027 Admission Requirements Prospective students applying for Fall 2027 admission must complete the UNC Graduate School application and select Public Policy as their intended program. According to UNC Public Policy s admissions instructions, applicants are required to provide supplemental application materials including: 1. Statement of Purpose Applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose as part of the online application. This is an important component of a doctoral application and provides applicants with an opportunity to explain their academic and research interests and reasons for pursuing advanced study in public policy. 2. Three Letters of Recommendation Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation . UNC specifies that at least two should normally come from faculty members familiar with the applicant s academic ability. For applicants who have accumulated substantial professional experience after college, letters from individuals capable of describing the applicant s potential to succeed in doctoral-level work may be substituted. GRE Is Not Required for Fall 2027 A particularly important point for applicants is that GRE scores will not be required or reviewed for the 2027 admissions cycle . Applicants therefore do not need to submit GRE scores for consideration under the stated Fall 2027 Public Policy admissions requirements. English Language Requirements for International Applicants The program is open to international applicants, but applicants subject to UNC s international English-language testing requirements need to pay close attention to the accepted tests. According to the admissions information provided, international applicants must submit acceptable official scores from either: TOEFL , reported directly from ETS; or IELTS , reported directly from IELTS. UNC states that no other English-language tests are accepted under these requirements. The stated minimum total scores are: Internet-based TOEFL: 90 IELTS: 7 International applicants should review UNC Graduate School s complete international applicant instructions to determine how these testing rules apply to their individual circumstances. Application Deadline for Fall 2027 The application deadline for the UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy for Fall 2027 admission is: December 1, 2026 Prospective applicants should not wait until the deadline to begin preparing their applications. Doctoral applications require substantial preparation, particularly because applicants must coordinate recommendation letters, prepare a strong Statement of Purpose, gather academic information and, where applicable, arrange official TOEFL or IELTS scores. International applicants should allow additional time for official English-language test reporting. How to Apply for the UNC PhD in Public Policy 2027 Applications must be completed online through the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Graduate School . Applicants should: Visit the UNC Graduate School degree programs/application website. Locate and select Public Policy from the relevant program options. Complete the online graduate application. Upload the required Statement of Purpose. Arrange for three Letters of Recommendation. Complete all additional Graduate School application requirements. If applicable, arrange for official TOEFL or IELTS scores to be submitted according to UNC s instructions. Review the application carefully for completeness. Submit the completed application by December 1, 2026 . Application/Program Information: https://publicpolicy.unc.edu/admissions/ UNC Graduate School: https://gradschool.unc.edu/academics/degreeprograms/ Applicants should always review the official Graduate School and UNC Public Policy pages before submitting an application because university requirements, procedures and supporting documentation may be subject to change. Important Considerations Before Applying A PhD is a substantial academic commitment, and prospective applicants should carefully consider whether the UNC Public Policy program aligns with their research interests and career objectives. Potential applicants may particularly want to evaluate: How their proposed research interests align with UNC Public Policy faculty expertise. Which substantive policy field they might eventually pursue. Their preparation in quantitative methods, statistics, economics and research design. Their readiness for intensive doctoral-level research. Their long-term academic, policy or research career objectives. Funding arrangements and the expected duration of doctoral study. English-language testing requirements if applying internationally. The availability of faculty members whose research overlaps with their intended specialization. Because doctoral education involves close collaboration with academic advisors and faculty committees, research alignment can be an important consideration when evaluating a PhD program. APPLY NOW Contact for Questions About the Application Applicants with questions concerning application requirements or the admissions process can contact the Student Services representative listed by UNC Public Policy: Meredith Albright Student Services The PhD Program, UNC Public Policy University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Campus Box #3435, Abernethy Hall Chapel Hill, NC 27599-3435 United States Email: merealb@unc.edu Telephone: (919) 962-1600 Conclusion The UNC Chapel Hill PhD in Public Policy 2027 provides an opportunity for aspiring scholars, researchers and policy professionals to undertake rigorous interdisciplinary doctoral training at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Through a combination of public policy theory, economics, political science, normative analysis, research design, quantitative methods and individualized policy specialization, the program is structured to prepare students to conduct independent research addressing important domestic and global policy problems. Students progress from intensive coursework to a specialized policy field, an independent field paper, a dissertation proposal and ultimately an original doctoral dissertation. The ability to develop expertise in areas ranging from education and labor markets to health, immigration, environmental policy, international development and global health gives students considerable scope to align their doctoral training with their long-term research interests. The absence of a GRE requirement for the Fall 2027 admissions cycle may also make the application process more accessible to prospective candidates. International applicants can apply, although those subject to English-language testing requirements must meet UNC s TOEFL or IELTS requirements. Prospective students interested in research-intensive careers in academia, government, policy organizations, non-profits or related fields should carefully review the program, identify potential areas of research alignment and begin preparing their application well before the deadline. Applications for Fall 2027 admission must be submitted by December 1, 2026. Visit the OFY website for more Scholarship Opportunities . title: ACET Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program 2026: Six-Month Opportunity Supporting Gender Equality and Women’s Economic Empowerment in Africa
summary: The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program 2026 is an opportunity for graduates interested in gender equality, women’s economic empowerment, development policy, research and programme management to gain practical professional experience while contributing to programmes focused on advancing gender equality across Africa. ACET is recruiting a motivated Graduate Intern for its Gender Equality Program (GEP) to provide programme coordination and delivery support across a portfolio of initiatives. The successful candidate will also contribute to research, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), procurement, stakeholder engagement and general programme administration. The internship is particularly relevant for graduates from fields such as gender studies, economics, development studies, public policy and the social sciences who want to strengthen their professional experience while working on issues affecting gender equality and economic transformation in Africa. Applications must be submitted by Thursday, 17 September 2026 . The internship will initially run for six months, with the possibility of an extension depending on the intern’s performance and the needs of the programme. About the African Center for Economic Transformation The African Center for Economic Transformation works on issues connected to Africa’s economic transformation and development. Its areas of work include economic management and governance, gender equality, green industrial transformation, innovation and digital policy, private-sector development, regional integration, and youth employment and skills. Through the Gender Equality Program, ACET maintains a portfolio of programmes and projects designed to advance gender equality and women’s economic empowerment across Africa . The current Gender Equality Program portfolio includes: African Women’s Inclusion Index (AWII) Shared Power Care Economy in Africa Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB) Gender Mainstreaming These initiatives form the broader environment in which the selected graduate intern will work and provide programme support. About the ACET Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program 2026 The Graduate Intern will support the coordination and delivery of activities across ACET’s Gender Equality Program portfolio. One of the central purposes of the position is to improve visibility and coordination across GEP’s different workstreams by ensuring that reliable and up-to-date information is maintained concerning programme activities, deadlines, deliverables and outstanding actions. Rather than being limited to one narrow function, the internship covers several aspects of programme implementation. The successful candidate will have opportunities to contribute to programme coordination, research, MEL, procurement, stakeholder engagement, events and programme administration. Because several tasks and projects may be taking place simultaneously, ACET is looking for a graduate who is highly organised, proactive and capable of managing multiple responsibilities. The successful candidate should also communicate effectively with colleagues across different teams and be comfortable working with limited day-to-day supervision. Key Responsibilities of the Graduate Intern The selected intern will undertake responsibilities across six major areas. 1. Programme and Workplan Coordination Programme coordination will form an important part of the internship. The intern will help the GEP team maintain visibility over its various activities and deadlines by keeping the programme tracker updated. This will include information relating to: Programme activities Key milestones Deliverables Responsible team members Deadlines The intern will also prepare short weekly overviews identifying upcoming deadlines, overdue tasks and matters requiring the team’s attention. Another responsibility will involve following up with relevant team members concerning outstanding actions. This means the intern will need to communicate proactively and ensure that important activities do not remain unresolved without appropriate follow-up. The intern will additionally monitor GEP’s work with other ACET functions, including Finance, Procurement, MEL and Communications. Support will also be provided for GEP team planning and programme review meetings. 2. Procurement and Consultant Coordination The internship provides exposure to procurement and consultant management processes within a development-focused organisation. The successful candidate will support the preparation, submission and tracking of procurement requests and their supporting documentation. The intern will liaise with the Procurement team to follow up on routine requirements and timelines, helping ensure that programme-related procurement activities move forward as required. The intern will also provide support during consultant recruitment and contracting processes. Responsibilities may include: Coordinating interviews Supporting shortlisting processes Coordinating feedback Tracking consultant contracts Monitoring consultant deliverables against agreed timelines This aspect of the internship can provide useful experience for graduates interested in programme administration, project management and international development operations. 3. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning and Programme Reporting Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, commonly referred to as MEL, is another important component of the internship. The intern will assist with collecting and consolidating information needed for quarterly MEL reporting. Information may relate to: Programme activities Outputs Events Stakeholder engagements Cross-team collaborations The successful candidate will also maintain relevant records and trackers throughout each reporting period. In addition, the intern will follow up with project leads to help ensure that required inputs are submitted on time for MEL and other programme reporting requirements. 4. Programme and Research Support Graduates interested in research and policy will also have opportunities to support research activities associated with GEP’s programmes. Responsibilities may include conducting targeted literature and evidence searches and helping prepare research summaries. The intern may also support: Organisation of datasets and research materials where appropriate References and research documentation Background research ahead of policy engagements Short policy-facing outputs where appropriate This combination of research and programme responsibilities makes the internship particularly relevant to candidates seeking practical exposure to the relationship between evidence, policy engagement and programme implementation. 5. Events and Stakeholder Coordination The Graduate Intern will also contribute to stakeholder engagement and event coordination. The successful candidate will help plan and coordinate GEP activities such as: Workshops Stakeholder meetings Validation sessions Dissemination events The intern will work with ACET’s Communications team and other relevant teams when coordinating these activities. Additional responsibilities will include participant coordination, preparing meeting materials, scheduling and conducting post-event follow-up. The intern may also prepare meeting notes and monitor outstanding actions arising from meetings or events. Maintaining stakeholder databases and engagement tracking will form another part of this responsibility. 6. General Programme Support Beyond the specific areas outlined above, the intern will provide general programme support to the Gender Equality Program. An important responsibility will be maintaining organised project documentation. The successful candidate will also support the effective flow of information between GEP projects and between the Gender Equality Program and other relevant ACET teams. Required Qualifications for the ACET Graduate Internship 2026 Candidates interested in applying should hold a relevant undergraduate or postgraduate degree . Relevant academic disciplines include: Gender studies Economics Development studies Public policy Social sciences Other related fields ACET is seeking candidates with strong organisational and coordination abilities. Applicants should demonstrate the capacity to manage several tasks and deadlines simultaneously. Candidates should also be proactive and detail-oriented. The role requires someone capable of anticipating requirements, following up on outstanding activities and identifying potential delays without requiring constant supervision. Applicants must also be proficient in Microsoft Excel and comfortable using digital tools for project tracking and documentation. Areas of Interest and Experience Applicants should demonstrate an interest in one or more areas related to the work of the Gender Equality Program, including: Gender equality Women’s economic empowerment Development policy Related development and policy issues Previous experience is not stated as an absolute requirement in the announcement. However, experience in certain areas will be considered an advantage. These include experience in: Programme coordination Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Research support Procurement processes Programme administration Candidates who have gained relevant experience through academic projects, internships, professional roles or related activities may therefore find their background relevant to the responsibilities of the position, although applicants should represent their experience accurately in their applications. Skills ACET Is Looking For The vacancy places considerable emphasis on organisation, initiative and the ability to coordinate multiple activities. An ideal applicant should therefore be able to demonstrate: Strong organisational ability: The role involves trackers, documentation, deliverables, meetings, deadlines and multiple projects. Coordination skills: The intern will interact with different teams and support activities involving Finance, Procurement, MEL, Communications and programme colleagues. Attention to detail: Accurate documentation, deadline tracking and reporting require careful attention to information. Proactivity: The intern is expected to follow up on outstanding actions and identify possible delays. Ability to work independently: ACET specifically seeks someone capable of working with limited day-to-day supervision. Digital competency: Applicants should be proficient in Excel and comfortable with digital project tracking and documentation tools. Interest in gender and development: Candidates should demonstrate genuine interest in gender equality, women’s economic empowerment, development policy or related areas. Duration of the ACET Gender Equality Program Internship The Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program position will initially run for six months . Importantly, ACET states that there is a possibility of extension . Any extension will depend on the intern’s performance and the needs of the programme. The selected intern will report directly to the Head of Gender Equality Program and will work closely with members of the GEP team across the programme’s portfolio of projects. How to Apply for the ACET Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program 2026 Applicants must submit their applications by email. Candidates are required to prepare: An up-to-date CV A cover letter explaining why they are the most suitable candidate for the position Both documents should be emailed to: PnC@acetforafrica.org Applicants should use their cover letter to clearly connect their qualifications, skills and relevant experience with the requirements of the internship rather than simply repeating information already contained in their CV. The official vacancy announcement specifically requests a cover letter explaining why the applicant considers themselves the most suitable candidate for the position. Application Deadline The closing date for applications for the ACET Graduate Intern – Gender Equality Program 2026 is Thursday, 17 September 2026 . Applicants interested in the opportunity should prepare and submit their CV and cover letter before the closing date. ACET has also stated that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted . For graduates interested in development, gender policy and programme implementation, this internship provides exposure to several interconnected areas of professional work.
