title: Western Balkans Fund MOVE Grants 2026: Apply for Up to €3,000 for Regional Mobility, Cultural Exchange, Research and Professional Development
summary: The Western Balkans Fund (WBF) MOVE Grants 7th Open Call 2026 is now accepting applications from eligible individuals across the Western Balkans who are seeking financial support for short-term regional mobility, professional development, academic and scientific exchange, cultural cooperation, and sustainable development initiatives. Through the MOVE Grants Scheme, the Western Balkans Fund aims to strengthen people-to-people connections and regional cooperation by enabling individuals to travel beyond their country or place of residence to participate in meaningful learning, collaboration, exchange and representation opportunities. The programme is particularly relevant to artists, cultural professionals, researchers, scholars, journalists, youth workers, civil society activists, students, professionals and other changemakers who want to develop their skills, expand their networks and collaborate with individuals and institutions elsewhere in the Western Balkans. Successful applicants can request between €500 and €3,000 , with the Western Balkans Fund able to cover up to 100% of eligible costs associated with an approved mobility activity. Applications for the 7th Open Call must be submitted by 5 October 2026 at 12:59 CET . About the Western Balkans Fund MOVE Grants Scheme The Western Balkans Fund developed the MOVE Grants mechanism around the principle that direct, in-person interaction can play an important role in strengthening trust, mutual understanding and shared values across the Western Balkans. The Western Balkans region covered by the programme consists of six WBF Contracting Parties: Albania Bosnia and Herzegovina Kosovo Montenegro North Macedonia Serbia Despite progress in regional cooperation, the Western Balkans continues to face challenges surrounding social cohesion, connectivity and deeper regional integration. MOVE Grants seek to contribute to addressing these challenges by making relatively small and accessible mobility grants available directly to individuals. Rather than focusing solely on large organisations and institutional projects, the scheme enables individual professionals, students and changemakers to pursue short-term opportunities that can produce meaningful professional and regional connections. The programme therefore places considerable emphasis on mobility, exchange and people-to-people cooperation. What Is the Main Objective of the MOVE Grants? The overall objective of the MOVE Grants Scheme is to foster regional cooperation in the Western Balkans by supporting individual mobility initiatives that promote: Academic exchange; Cultural exchange; Professional exchange; Regional collaboration; Learning and skills development; Knowledge sharing; Networking and partnership building; and Representation of the Western Balkans in relevant regional and international settings. Through short-term and needs-based opportunities for collaboration, representation and learning, the Western Balkans Fund seeks to strengthen people-to-people connections and cultivate a stronger regional mindset. The broader ambition is to empower individuals to become agents of positive change while contributing towards a more inclusive, equitable and interconnected Western Balkans. How Much Funding Is Available? The overall financial envelope available under the MOVE Grants 7th Open Call is €40,000 . Individual applicants can request: Minimum grant: €500 Maximum grant: €3,000 The Western Balkans Fund may finance up to 100% of the total eligible costs of an approved mobility action. Cost-sharing or co-financing is also permitted where applicable. Applicants should develop realistic budgets based on genuine expected costs in the market. The budget should be prepared in euros and clearly connected to the proposed mobility activity. Only costs presented in the submitted budget will be considered for financing. Who Are MOVE Grants Designed to Support? MOVE Grants are intended for a diverse group of individuals from across the Western Balkans. Potential applicants include both young and senior professionals, such as: Individual artists; Cultural professionals; Researchers; Scholars; Journalists; Youth workers; Civil society organisation activists; Students; Established professionals; Professionals affiliated with public or non-public organisations; and Other changemakers whose mobility aligns with the objectives of the programme. Only individual applications are eligible. The programme does not support applications seeking funding for the mobility of groups of people travelling together. Applicant Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all eligibility conditions established by the Western Balkans Fund. To qualify, an applicant must: Be at least 18 years old on the application deadline. Be both a citizen and resident of one of the six Western Balkans Contracting Parties. Be an established professional, be employed or affiliated with a legal public or non-public organisation, or be currently enrolled as a student at the application deadline. Have no criminal record. Be capable of preparing the application, communicating with the Western Balkans Fund and reporting on the mobility activity in English. Applicants should carefully assess these requirements before beginning an application. Mobility Must Involve Regional Movement An important feature of the programme is that MOVE Grants are intended to facilitate genuine mobility and exchange. Activities should primarily take place within the Western Balkans and involve mobility to one or more WBF Contracting Parties other than the one in which the applicant is based. Mobility taking place solely within an applicant s own place of residence is not supported. For example, an eligible applicant based in Albania could potentially undertake an appropriate mobility activity involving a host institution in Montenegro, Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina or Kosovo, subject to all other requirements being satisfied. Can Mobility Take Place Outside the Western Balkans? The programme primarily supports activities within the Western Balkans. However, activities outside the region may be considered in exceptional and justified circumstances , particularly when taking place within the European Union. Such international mobility must contribute to the visibility and promotion of the Western Balkans within relevant international contexts. Applicants proposing an activity outside the Western Balkans should therefore be able to clearly demonstrate why the international dimension is justified and how the proposed mobility will benefit or represent the region. Applicants Must Have a Host Institution MOVE Grants require applicants to establish a formal relationship with a host institution . This is an important eligibility requirement because the partnership demonstrates that the proposed mobility is legitimate, relevant and practically feasible. For regional mobility, the activity must normally involve at least two WBF Contracting Parties: The Contracting Party in which the applicant resides; and The Contracting Party where the host institution is established. Applicants must provide formal and verifiable evidence demonstrating the partnership. Acceptable evidence can include: An official invitation letter from the host institution confirming the applicant s invitation for a particular period and purpose; or Confirmed registration, acceptance or an appropriate letter demonstrating enrolment or participation in a programme, course or workshop organised by the host institution. An official invitation or other required evidence of participation must be included in the application package. Three Main Areas of Intervention Applications must align with the mission of the Western Balkans Fund and the objectives of the MOVE Grants Call. Proposals should address one or more of three principal areas: 1. Cultural Cooperation Cultural cooperation activities should help build bridges across cultural differences and encourage partnerships that contribute to regional peace, cohesion and cooperation. Examples can include: Participating in regional cultural festivals, exhibitions or performances; Showcasing artistic and cultural heritage; Joint theatre, film, music and visual arts productions; Artist residencies; Cultural exchange programmes; Intercultural dialogue workshops and seminars; Youth-led cultural forums; Digital cultural platforms; Multimedia projects promoting regional culture; Cultural workshops and professional training; Storytelling and oral history projects; Cultural documentation initiatives; and Regional sports or cultural exchanges that encourage youth engagement and cultural interaction. This area may be particularly relevant to artists, filmmakers, musicians, cultural workers and other creative professionals seeking opportunities to collaborate across borders. 2. Education and Scientific Exchanges The education and scientific exchange component seeks to enhance regional cooperation in education and research. Mobility activities can focus on capacity building, professional and academic exchange, scientific collaboration and knowledge development. Examples include: Short-term research exchanges at universities; Research centre or laboratory exchanges; Workshops; Seminars; Training courses; Professional development programmes; Academic internships; Professional internships and work placements; Attendance at regional conferences and symposiums; Presenting research at academic events; Joint scientific research; Joint publications involving partners from different Western Balkans Contracting Parties; Development of innovative educational programmes; Curriculum development; Field research; Data collection; and Academic and scientific networking and partnership building. Students, academics, researchers and other professionals seeking to strengthen their expertise through regional exchange may therefore find significant opportunities under this intervention area. 3. Sustainable Development The sustainable development component focuses on mobility activities capable of supporting regional cohesion and long-term prosperity. Projects may address sustainable economic growth, environmental stewardship, social inclusion and institutional cooperation. Potential activities include: Joint institutional partnerships; Collaborative sustainable economic development projects; Environmental research; Climate change mitigation initiatives; Biodiversity preservation; Natural resource management; Sustainability-focused training and workshops; Capacity-building programmes; Study visits; Internships or work placements with organisations involved in sustainability or the green economy; Social inclusion programmes; Initiatives empowering marginalised groups; Community development programmes; Regional sustainable development conferences; Environmental governance forums; Policy dialogues; Field research; Sustainability-related data collection; Collaborative advocacy; and Policy development supporting sustainable practices. Cross-Cutting Priorities Applicants are encouraged to integrate important cross-cutting priorities into their mobility proposals. These include: Gender equality; Human rights; Inclusion of minorities and vulnerable groups; Environmental sustainability and climate action; Democracy and rule of law; Digitalisation and innovation; and Youth engagement. Applicants should take these priorities seriously because the integration of cross-cutting issues forms part of the evaluation process. What Expenses Can the MOVE Grant Cover? Funding can cover several categories of direct costs that are necessary for implementing the mobility activity. Transportation Eligible transportation expenses can include: Flights; Trains; Buses; Shuttle services; Taxis; Personal car travel directly related to the mobility; Toll roads; and Parking when travelling by personal car. Travel arrangements should follow the principle of selecting the most cost-effective and economical option available. Where an eligible applicant uses a personal vehicle, mileage reimbursement may be calculated at €0.30 per kilometre . Health Insurance and Visa Costs Where applicable, funding may cover: Medical or travel insurance required for the stay; and Eligible visa costs associated with regional mobility. Accommodation Accommodation expenses may be supported when directly associated with the approved mobility. Examples include: Hotels; Hostels; and Bed and Breakfast accommodation. Accommodation must be cost-efficient and consistent with local market rates. The maximum accommodation calculation is: €65 per night within the Western Balkans region €80 per night outside the Western Balkans Daily Allowance Applicants may budget a daily allowance of €40 per day to help cover meals and incidental expenses. The allowance should only apply to eligible activity and travel days. Where travel takes less than six hours and qualifies as half-day travel, half of the daily allowance should be calculated. Special Needs Support Additional costs may be considered where necessary to enable the full participation of applicants with disabilities. This can potentially include: Mobility assistance; Specialised transportation; and Accessible accommodation. Registration and Participation Fees Registration fees may be eligible when required to participate in an approved activity, including: Conferences; Training programmes; Workshops; and Residencies. Visibility Costs Applicants can potentially allocate up to 7% of the total requested budget towards visibility costs associated with promoting their mobility activity and communicating its impact to relevant audiences. Postal and Courier Costs Postal or courier expenses directly related to required documents, reports, correspondence or materials may also be eligible. Costs That Cannot Be Funded Applicants should avoid including expenses that are not permitted under the scheme. Ineligible costs include: Costs incurred outside the contractual period, subject to specified exceptions for confirmed registration payments; Salaries and other human-resource expenses; External expertise or consultancy fees; Indirect costs; Expenses receiving double funding; Personal expenses unrelated to the mobility; Debts and interest payments; Provisions for future losses or liabilities; Profit-making activities; Activities affiliated with political or religious agendas; Currency exchange losses; Subcontracting; Entertainment or leisure expenses; and Fines, penalties or legal charges resulting from non-compliance with laws or regulations. When Must the Mobility Take Place? Successful mobility activities must be implemented between: December 2026 and April 2027. The final report must be completed within the contractual implementation period and no later than 30 April 2027 . Applicants should therefore develop a realistic activity schedule that can be completed within this timeframe. How to Apply for the WBF MOVE Grants 2026 Applications must be completed in English and submitted electronically through the Western Balkans Fund s Online Grant Management System (OGMS). Applicants need to prepare a complete application containing: Application Form – completed through the OGMS. Budget – completed within the online system. Declaration by the Applicant – signed and uploaded. Formal evidence of the proposed mobility – such as the required invitation or confirmation documentation, signed and uploaded where applicable. Applicants should register and apply through the official WBF Applicant Portal: https://wbfportal.org/applicants After submission, applicants should receive an automatic confirmation email containing a protocol number. If no confirmation email is received within 48 hours, applicants are advised to contact the Western Balkans Fund. Application Deadline The deadline for submitting applications for the Western Balkans Fund MOVE Grants 7th Open Call is: 5 October 2026 at 12:59 CET Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered. Candidates are strongly encouraged not to wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Deadline for Questions and Clarifications Applicants who have questions about the guidelines or application procedure may submit written enquiries to: info@westernbalkansfund.org The email subject should contain: Q: MOVE Grants Applications The deadline for submitting questions is 25 September 2026 . WBF is not obligated to respond to questions received after the clarification deadline, and enquiries must be submitted in writing rather than by telephone. How Will Applications Be Evaluated? Applications undergo a multi-stage evaluation process. Step 1: Administrative and Eligibility Checks The Western Balkans Fund will first determine whether the applicant and application satisfy fundamental requirements. Checks include whether: The applicant is at least 18; Citizenship and residency requirements are satisfied; The application was submitted before the deadline; The applicant has submitted only one application; The applicant does not already hold an active MOVE Grant; The proposed activity fits within the permitted implementation timeframe; The required regional mobility dimension is present; The requested budget does not exceed €3,000; The applicant declaration has been completed and signed; The required invitation or confirmation from the host institution has been provided; and The application is prepared in English and submitted through the OGMS. Missing, incomplete or incorrect documentation can result in rejection before the proposal reaches technical evaluation. Step 2: Technical Evaluation Applications that successfully pass the initial eligibility checks will undergo technical assessment. Proposals can receive a maximum of 100 points . The evaluation considers areas including: Quality and coherence of the mobility proposal; Whether activities are realistic and achievable; Clarity of roles; Regional relevance; Contribution to the objectives of MOVE Grants; Potential for personal growth; Expected impact; Sustainability and follow-up; Introduction of innovative or new practices; Integration of cross-cutting priorities; Financial planning and value for money; and Communication and visibility. Applications scoring less than 55 points on the ranking list will not be recommended for further consideration by the Evaluation Panel. Step 3: Evaluation Panel Following technical evaluation, high-ranking proposals are presented to the WBF Evaluation Panel. The panel reviews and endorses the ranking resulting from the technical assessment. This stage is followed by relevant negotiation, monitoring planning and the final processes associated with selecting, training and contracting successful grantees. Step 4: Verification for Provisionally Selected Applicants Applicants provisionally selected for funding will be required to submit additional supporting documentation within 10 working days . Documents can include: A copy of a government-issued passport or identity card; Official confirmation that the applicant has no criminal record; Confirmation from an employer or organisation verifying the applicant s employment or involvement, where applicable; and A partnership agreement between home and host organisations where applicable. WBF will compare these supporting documents against the information and declarations contained in the application. Missing documents or inconsistencies can result in rejection. Funding Decision and Notification Applicants will be notified of the outcome by email. The indicative timetable states that the funding decision should be communicated no later than 25 November 2026 . Successful applicants will receive formal notification following the funding decision. Applicants who believe there was an irregularity in the evaluation process may submit a written request for clarification within seven calendar days after receiving the official notification. How Will Successful Applicants Receive the Grant? Following selection, the approved mobility budget will be reviewed before contracting. Where costs are considered ineligible or insufficiently justified, WBF may reduce the approved amount and explain the reasons for the adjustment. Once the grant agreement is signed by both the applicant and WBF, the successful applicant officially becomes a beneficiary of the MOVE Grants Scheme. Funding is then provided in two instalments: 70% pre-payment following submission of the required documents and signing of the grant contract. 30% remaining balance following submission and approval of the required final documentation, including eligible invoices and receipts. Payments are made in euros to the bank account specified in the grant contract. Important Dates for MOVE Grants 2026 Applicants should take note of the following indicative timeline: Call opens: 4 September 2026 Information session: 11 September 2026 at 11:00 CET Deadline for clarification requests: 25 September 2026 Application deadline: 5 October 2026 at 12:59 CET Application evaluation: Within approximately 30 working days after the deadline Funding decision: No later than 25 November 2026 Contracting: Within approximately 15 working days following notification Mobility implementation: December 2026 to April 2027 Final reporting deadline: No later than 30 April 2027 Applicants should note that the timetable is indicative and may be updated by the Western Balkans Fund during the procedure. Why the WBF MOVE Grants 2026 Opportunity Matters The MOVE Grants Scheme offers more than financial assistance for travel. Its focus is on creating purposeful mobility that leads to professional development, knowledge exchange, collaboration and stronger relationships across the Western Balkans. For an artist, it could mean participating in a residency or collaborating with creatives elsewhere in the region. For a researcher or student, it could support a research visit, academic event, training opportunity or scientific exchange. For a journalist, activist, youth worker or civil society professional, it could provide access to regional networking, professional development or collaborative initiatives. For professionals working on sustainability, the funding could support participation in research, training, policy dialogue, fieldwork or projects dealing with environmental and social challenges. The central requirement is that the mobility should have a clear purpose and contribute meaningfully to regional cooperation. APPLY NOW Conclusion The Western Balkans Fund MOVE Grants 7th Open Call 2026 provides a valuable funding opportunity for individuals seeking to learn, collaborate, conduct research, develop professionally or share their work across the Western Balkans. With grants ranging from €500 to €3,000 and funding of up to 100% of eligible costs , the programme can help remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent individuals from accessing valuable regional opportunities. Artists, researchers, students, journalists, cultural professionals, youth workers, civil society activists and other professionals who have an eligible mobility opportunity should carefully review the requirements, secure appropriate confirmation from a host institution and develop a realistic proposal demonstrating regional relevance and meaningful impact. Applications must be submitted through the WBF Online Grant Management System by 5 October 2026 at 12:59 CET . Visit the OFY website for more Grant Opportunities . title: EGEN Research Prize 2026: Win Up to $3,000 for Cutting-Edge Research on Gender and Politics
summary: The EGEN Research Prize 2026 , presented by EGEN in collaboration with Johns Hopkins University , is now accepting applications from graduate students and very early career scholars conducting innovative empirical research on gender and politics . The research prize is designed to recognize and encourage emerging scholars producing high-quality, original research that advances understanding of gender and political issues. The organisers support empirical scholarship across a wide range of methodological approaches and academic subfields, with particular interest in developing research in comparative politics and international relations . Selected researchers will receive financial awards ranging from $1,000 to $3,000 , while several additional applicants will receive $500 honorable mentions . Winners will also receive an opportunity to be matched with a mentor from the EGEN executive board for the following year. About the EGEN Research Prize The EGEN Research Prize is part of EGEN s efforts to support and recognize junior scholars working on important questions surrounding gender and politics. The prize focuses on empirical gender scholarship , meaning research that uses evidence and systematic research approaches to examine political questions related to gender. The organisers welcome research across different methodological approaches and subfields rather than limiting applicants to one particular research method. This makes the prize potentially relevant to researchers working with: Quantitative research Qualitative research Mixed-method research Comparative research International relations research Political science research Other empirical approaches to studying gender and politics The organisers are particularly interested in encouraging emerging work in comparative politics and international relations . EGEN Research Prize 2026 Awards Successful applicants can receive one of several financial prizes. Main Research Prizes Several selected researchers will receive awards ranging from: $1,000 to $3,000 The exact amount awarded may vary among the selected prize recipients. Honorable Mentions In addition to the main prizes, several applicants will receive: $500 honorable mentions These awards provide additional recognition for promising research that demonstrates quality, innovation and relevance to the field. Mentorship Opportunity for Winners One of the notable benefits of the EGEN Research Prize is that winners are not only recognized financially. Prize winners will also be matched with a mentor from the EGEN executive board for the coming year . This provides an opportunity for emerging scholars to receive guidance and build a professional relationship with an established member of the EGEN leadership network. For graduate students and very early career researchers, mentorship can be valuable for developing research ideas, strengthening academic work and navigating the early stages of an academic career. Research Areas of Interest The 2026 prize focuses on gender and politics . Applicants should therefore submit research that makes a meaningful contribution to understanding the relationship between gender and political processes, institutions, behaviour, outcomes or international affairs. The organisers support research across methodological approaches and subfields. However, particular interest is placed on research that can help incubate emerging scholarship in: Comparative Politics Research may examine political processes and gender-related questions across countries, political systems or societies. International Relations Research may explore gender within international political institutions, global political processes, international security, diplomacy, conflict, foreign policy or other areas of international relations. Applicants should ensure that their research clearly demonstrates its relevance to gender and politics. Who Can Apply? The EGEN Research Prize is intended specifically for: Graduate students Very early career scholars The opportunity is therefore aimed at researchers who are still in the early stages of their academic careers rather than established senior academics. Graduate students should provide their advisor s contact information as part of the application process. APPLY HERE Coauthored Research Coauthored work is eligible for consideration. However, there is an important condition: Every co-author must also be eligible for the prize. Applicants submitting coauthored research should therefore ensure that all individuals listed as co-authors meet the eligibility requirements for graduate students or very early career scholars. Original Research and AI Requirement The submitted work must be original . The organisers specifically state that submissions must not be generated by AI . Applicants should therefore submit their own original research and writing and ensure that their work complies with the prize s requirements concerning originality and authorship. What Applicants Must Submit Applicants are required to submit several materials as part of the 2026 application. 1. Application Form Applicants must complete the official EGEN Research Prize application form. The application form collects the information required for consideration and also asks applicants to identify potential mentors. 2. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide their CV as a PDF. The file should be named: lastname_firstname_CV.pdf Applicants should ensure that the CV clearly presents their academic background, research experience, publications and other relevant scholarly achievements. 3. Anonymized Writing Sample Applicants must submit an anonymized version of their most polished piece of writing . The writing sample must be provided as a PDF and should be named: lastname_firstname_writing sample.pdf The sample should be anonymized, meaning identifying information should be removed where appropriate so that the research can be evaluated without unnecessary identifying details. Applicants should choose a piece of work that best demonstrates the quality of their research, writing and analytical abilities. 4. Advisor Contact Information Graduate students must provide their advisor s contact information . This information is entered directly into the application form. How the Documents Are Submitted There are two different submission processes that applicants need to pay attention to. The application form is completed online, while the CV and writing sample are uploaded separately through a Dropbox file request. Applicants must therefore make sure they complete both parts of the submission process. The application form asks applicants to confirm that they have uploaded both required documents. Failure to complete the document-upload portion could result in an incomplete application. Potential Mentors The application form also asks applicants to identify three potential mentors from the EGEN executive board , either past or present. Applicants should therefore review the EGEN executive board and select three potential mentors whose academic interests or expertise are relevant to their research. Choosing appropriate mentors can help demonstrate that the applicant has considered how mentorship could support the development of their research and academic career. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2026 EGEN Research Prize is: 15 October 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET). Applicants should submit all required materials before the deadline and should not wait until the final hours to upload their documents. Submission Language All submissions must be made in: English Applicants should ensure that their application materials and submitted writing sample meet this language requirement. How to Apply Applicants should follow these steps: Complete the official EGEN Research Prize application form. Prepare a current CV in PDF format. Name the CV according to the required format: lastname_firstname_CV.pdf . Select your most polished research or writing work. Anonymize the writing sample. Save the writing sample as a PDF. Name it according to the required format: lastname_firstname_writing sample.pdf . Upload both the CV and anonymized writing sample through the designated Dropbox file request. Confirm in the application form that both documents have been uploaded. Graduate students should provide their advisor s contact information. Identify three potential mentors from the EGEN executive board, past or present. Submit the completed application before 15 October 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET . Visit HERE to learn more about the EGEN Research Prize 2026 Important Application Requirements Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully review the following requirements: The applicant must be a graduate student or very early career scholar. The research must focus on gender and politics. Empirical research is encouraged. Multiple methodological approaches and subfields are supported. Comparative politics and international relations research is particularly encouraged. Submissions must be in English. The work must be original and must not be generated by AI. Coauthored work is permitted only when every co-author is eligible. Graduate students must provide advisor contact information. A CV must be submitted as a PDF. An anonymized writing sample must be submitted as a PDF. The CV and writing sample must be uploaded through the specified Dropbox file request. Applicants must identify three potential mentors from the EGEN executive board. The application must be submitted by the stated deadline. Why Researchers Should Consider Applying The EGEN Research Prize offers more than financial recognition. For emerging scholars, receiving a research prize can provide recognition for their academic work while also creating opportunities to develop professional connections within the field. The combination of financial awards, academic recognition and mentorship makes the opportunity particularly relevant to graduate students and researchers at the beginning of their careers. The prize can also provide encouragement for scholars developing innovative research on gender and politics, particularly those working in comparative politics and international relations. Conclusion The 2026 EGEN Research Prize provides an opportunity for graduate students and very early career scholars to gain recognition and financial support for innovative research on gender and politics . With several awards ranging from $1,000 to $3,000 , additional $500 honorable mentions , and a mentorship opportunity with members of the EGEN executive board, the prize offers both financial and professional-development value to emerging researchers. Applicants should ensure that their research aligns with the focus on gender and politics, carefully prepare their CV and anonymized writing sample, follow the required file-naming and submission procedures, and identify three potential EGEN mentors. For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org. summary: Applications are now open for Youth Pavilion side events at CBD COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia , providing an opportunity for young people, youth groups, networks, youth-led organisations and partners to propose and host interactive events as part of the Youth Pavilion programme. The initiative is designed to create space for young people to amplify their voices, exchange experiences, build connections and bring forward issues and ideas that matter to youth during COP17 . Applicants with creative and engaging ideas are invited to propose events that can contribute to discussions, knowledge sharing and youth participation at the Youth Pavilion. About the COP17 Youth Pavilion Side Events The Youth Pavilion at CBD COP17 is intended to provide a dedicated space for youth voices and participation. The call invites young people and youth-focused organisations to propose an interactive side event that they would like to bring to the Youth Pavilion during COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia. The opportunity is open to a range of potential applicants, including: Young people Youth groups Youth networks Youth-led organisations Partners with relevant ideas for an event Applicants are encouraged to develop activities that promote interaction, dialogue, learning, creativity, networking and knowledge exchange. Possible formats highlighted in the opportunity include: Intergenerational Dialogues Applicants can propose discussions that bring together people from different generations to exchange perspectives, experiences and ideas. Cultural Activities and Artivism The Youth Pavilion can also feature cultural activities and artivism, providing opportunities to communicate environmental and biodiversity issues through creative and cultural expression. Workshops and Interactive Sessions Applicants may organise workshops or other interactive sessions that encourage participants to actively engage with a topic rather than simply listen to presentations. Panel Discussions Panel discussions can provide a platform for different speakers to explore issues relevant to young people, biodiversity and the broader COP17 agenda. Networking and Knowledge Sharing Proposed events can also focus on connecting participants, sharing experiences and exchanging knowledge among young people, organisations and other stakeholders. Other Creative Formats The call also welcomes other creative formats that can contribute meaningfully to the Youth Pavilion programme. Purpose of the Youth Pavilion The Youth Pavilion is presented as a space where young people can amplify their voices and participate more actively in discussions at COP17.
